foundations-functions.name: Function and fiber machine
foundations-functions.question: How does changing one function value change a fiber?
foundations-functions.prediction: Which fiber loses an input and which gains it if f(0) changes from 0 to 1?
foundations-functions.objects: A function from X={0,1,2,3,4,5} to Y={0,1,2}; input equivalence is congruence modulo m.
foundations-functions.invariant: Every input has exactly one output; the nonempty fibers partition X.
foundations-functions.counterexample: Choose incompatible representatives to see why a function need not descend to chosen classes.
foundations-functions.debrief: The arrow diagram displays a finite function. Existence of a general descended map follows from representative independence, proved in the lesson.
foundations-functions.fallback: All essential values are listed as labelled text and tables below the controls.

foundations-fibers.name: Fiber partition constructor
foundations-fibers.question: Can two different nonempty fibers overlap?
foundations-fibers.prediction: Change f(4) to 0: predict the sizes of the fibers of 0 and 1.
foundations-fibers.objects: Six inputs, three targets, and equality-of-output fibers. The independently chosen input classes need not be fibers.
foundations-fibers.invariant: Each input occurs in one fiber. Empty fibers correspond to unused targets.
foundations-fibers.counterexample: Assign every input output 0; surjectivity fails but the nonempty fiber still partitions X.
foundations-fibers.debrief: Fibers partition the domain because a function assigns one output. Arbitrary congruence classes descend only when each lies inside a fiber.

foundations-quotient-rules.name: Quotient rule checker
foundations-quotient-rules.question: When does [x]↦f(x) survive a different representative?
foundations-quotient-rules.prediction: With f(x)=x mod 3 and parity input classes, compare representatives 0 and 2.
foundations-quotient-rules.objects: Domain quotient X/~, where ~ is congruence modulo m; the target Y is not quotiented.
foundations-quotient-rules.invariant: A well-defined map must be constant on each chosen input class.
foundations-quotient-rules.counterexample: The incompatible-representatives button uses parity classes with different function values.
foundations-quotient-rules.debrief: A finite witness disproves the proposed rule. Absence of a witness certifies only this displayed finite domain; the lesson proves the general criterion.

mh2220-axioms.name: Group operation and axiom checker
mh2220-axioms.question: Does this closed operation actually form a group?
mh2220-axioms.prediction: Before choosing subtraction modulo 3, predict which axiom will fail.
mh2220-axioms.objects: Finite set {0,…,n−1}; operation choices are modular addition, multiplication, subtraction, or unreduced addition.
mh2220-axioms.invariant: Each axiom is tested separately; associativity compares every triple.
mh2220-axioms.counterexample: Subtraction exhibits an explicit associativity witness; unreduced addition exhibits failed closure.
mh2220-axioms.debrief: Exhaustive checks prove the axioms for the displayed finite operation. A family-wide result needs the algebraic proof in the lesson.

mh2220-inverse-order.name: Inverse and first-return experiment
mh2220-inverse-order.question: How many repeated generator steps return to identity?
mh2220-inverse-order.prediction: In C12 choose 8: will its order be 3, 6 or 12?
mh2220-inverse-order.objects: Additive Cn with a chosen residue generator and its additive inverse.
mh2220-inverse-order.invariant: A word evaluates by addition modulo n; the first positive return is n/gcd(n,g).
mh2220-inverse-order.counterexample: Choose 4 in C12: a nonzero element has order 3 and does not generate all 12 elements.
mh2220-inverse-order.debrief: Cyclic arithmetic is a concrete illustration. The inverse of an arbitrary noncommutative product still reverses factor order, as proved in the lesson.

mh2220-generators.question: Which elements can this generator reach?
mh2220-generators.prediction: For g=4 in C12, predict the entire reachable set before applying steps.
mh2220-generators.objects: Additive Cn, generator g, inverse −g, and words starting at 0.
mh2220-generators.invariant: Reachable points form the generated subgroup; a shortest word is recorded for each reachable element.
mh2220-generators.counterexample: A nonzero generator need not generate the whole cyclic group.
mh2220-generators.debrief: The finite search constructs this subgroup. It does not certify a presentation in another group; the lesson supplies the normal-form argument for S3.

mh2220-cyclic.name: Cyclic order and subgroup explorer
mh2220-cyclic.question: Which residues generate Cn?
mh2220-cyclic.prediction: Compare 4 and 5 in C12: which gives all twelve points?
mh2220-cyclic.objects: Finite cyclic group Z/nZ with addition and a chosen residue g.
mh2220-cyclic.invariant: The subgroup has n/gcd(n,g) elements and is all of Cn exactly when gcd(n,g)=1.
mh2220-cyclic.counterexample: Choose g=0 or a non-coprime residue to see a proper subgroup.
mh2220-cyclic.debrief: The table checks selected n. Divisibility proves the formula for every finite cyclic group, while the integer-exponent proof covers the infinite case.

mh2220-cosets.name: Coset partition constructor
mh2220-cosets.question: Do these representatives name the same left coset?
mh2220-cosets.prediction: For H={e,(12)}, predict whether (123)H equals H(123).
mh2220-cosets.objects: S3 acts on three letters; permutation products apply the right factor first.
mh2220-cosets.invariant: Cosets partition six elements into equal sets; equal size alone does not make sets equal.
mh2220-cosets.counterexample: The order-two subgroup has unequal left and right cosets.
mh2220-cosets.debrief: The tiling is a complete finite example. Translation h↦ah proves equal coset cardinality for arbitrary groups.

mh2220-normal.name: Normality and conjugation checker
mh2220-normal.question: Does conjugation preserve a subgroup as a set?
mh2220-normal.prediction: For A3, predict whether conjugating a 3-cycle by a transposition fixes that element or swaps it.
mh2220-normal.objects: S3, a chosen subgroup H and a conjugating permutation a; ab applies b first.
mh2220-normal.invariant: Normality is equality aHa⁻¹=H for every a, not pointwise fixation.
mh2220-normal.counterexample: The transposition subgroup moves to a different subgroup of the same size.
mh2220-normal.debrief: Left/right coset equality tests the same condition. The displayed checks are finite; the proof identifies all homomorphism kernels as normal.

mh2220-quotient.debrief: The witness rejects a nonnormal quotient. The expression anbm=ab(b⁻¹nb)m explains why normality makes the general law well-defined.

mh2220-actions.name: Group action workbench
mh2220-actions.question: How does changing the action change the orbit?
mh2220-actions.prediction: Compare the identity point under regular and conjugation actions.
mh2220-actions.objects: S3 acting on letters, on itself by left multiplication, or on itself by conjugation.
mh2220-actions.invariant: The identity acts trivially and (gh)·x=g·(h·x) for each action.
mh2220-actions.counterexample: Identity is fixed under conjugation but not under every regular-action element.
mh2220-actions.debrief: These are three different actions of one group. Orbit–stabilizer follows from a coset bijection, not merely from seeing equal products of counts.

actions-faithful-transitive.name: Faithfulness and transitivity checker
actions-faithful-transitive.question: Can an action be faithful without being transitive?
actions-faithful-transitive.prediction: For conjugation on S3, predict the kernel and the orbit of identity.
actions-faithful-transitive.objects: S3 acting on its elements by conjugation, or the natural and regular actions for comparison.
actions-faithful-transitive.invariant: Faithfulness uses the kernel on the whole set; transitivity compares one orbit with the whole set.
actions-faithful-transitive.counterexample: Conjugation on S3 is faithful but not transitive.
actions-faithful-transitive.debrief: The kernel is the center for conjugation; S3 has trivial center. One fixed point does not mean every group element acts trivially everywhere.

actions-stabilizer-kernel-core.name: Stabilizer, kernel and core inspector
actions-stabilizer-kernel-core.question: When is the core of a point stabilizer the whole action kernel?
actions-stabilizer-kernel-core.prediction: Choose identity under conjugation; compare its stabilizer core with the action kernel.
actions-stabilizer-kernel-core.objects: S3 with a left action; the core is the intersection of conjugates of the selected point stabilizer.
actions-stabilizer-kernel-core.invariant: The core is the kernel of the action restricted to that orbit.
actions-stabilizer-kernel-core.counterexample: At the identity conjugation orbit, the core is S3 while the whole-action kernel is {e}.
actions-stabilizer-kernel-core.debrief: For transitive actions the selected orbit is the whole set, so core and kernel agree. The distinction matters for nontransitive actions.
